# External Asset Credits

## Font — Fusion Pixel Font 缝合像素字体 (TakWolf)
- Source: https://github.com/TakWolf/fusion-pixel-font
- Author: TakWolf and contributors
- License: SIL Open Font License 1.1 — commercial use allowed, no RFN reserved
  (see assets/fonts/LICENSE-fusion-pixel-OFL-1.1.txt)
- Local: assets/fonts/fusion-pixel-12px-proportional-zh_hans.ttf
- Used: every glyph in the game. It is the default font of
  assets/ui/theme_rust.tres; sizes are locked to 12 / 24 / 36 because the
  design grid is 12px and a fractional multiple would resample the glyphs.
- Import: antialiasing = None, hinting = None, subpixel positioning = Disabled,
  mipmaps off, system fallback off — anything else softens the pixel edges.

## Font — Jacquard 24 (Tyler Finck / ETC)
- Source: https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Jacquard+24
- Author: Tyler Finck (ETC)
- License: SIL Open Font License 1.1 — commercial use allowed
  (see assets/fonts/LICENSE-Jacquard24-OFL-1.1.txt)
- Local: assets/fonts/Jacquard24-Regular.ttf
- Used: only offline, as the source for the blackletter "RUSTGRAVE" wordmark.
  tools/gen_ui_kit.py rasterizes it and hard-thresholds the coverage onto the
  design grid, so the shipped assets/ui/title_logo.png is pixel art rather than
  a scaled outline font.

## Pixel UI kit (project-original, procedurally drawn)
- Local: assets/ui/*.png, generated by tools/gen_ui_kit.py (PIL)
- License: part of this project.
- Every piece is drawn from the game palette on a 1x design grid and written
  out at 2x, so the borders read chunky next to 24px text and can only ever
  scale by whole pixels. Covers the 9-slice panels/buttons/meters, the heart
  sockets, the announcement ribbon, dividers, corner filigree, the bottom
  credit band, the blood vignette and the title wordmark.
- assets/ui/ember_motes.png is *derived*: tools/gen_ui_kit.py area-averages
  frames of CodeManu's CC0 brightfire sheet (see below) down to 6x6 and snaps
  them to the palette. Sampling that 100px source down at runtime made the
  motes vanish into the keyart.

## App icon (project-original, procedurally drawn)
- Local: icon.png (256x256) + icon.ico (16/32/48/64/128/256), generated by
  tools/gen_icon.py (PIL) from the same palette and frame helpers as the UI kit.
- License: part of this project.
- Drawn on a 16x16 grid and only ever upscaled by whole numbers, so every
  shipped size is the same art rather than a downsample. Deliberately *not*
  cropped from the title keyart: that keyart is AI-generated (see below), and
  the icon needed to be hand-drawn pixel art.

## Level01 / Level06 rust night plates (derived, project-original recolor)
- Local: assets/env/parallax_sky_rust.png, assets/env/parallax_mountains_rust.png,
  assets/env/parallax_clouds_rust.png, assets/env/parallax_clouds_low_rust.png
- Derived from the **GothicVania Cemetery Pack** (ansimuz) plates already listed
  above — same license chain, no new source: the originals are public domain
  ("credit is not required but appreciated" per the OGA notice, see
  gothicvania_cemetery/public-license.txt) and remain in assets/env untouched
  (parallax_sky.png / parallax_mountains.png / parallax_clouds_px.png /
  parallax_clouds_low_px.png are still shipped and are the runtime fallback if a
  derived plate is missing).
- Generated by tools/gen_theme_tiles.py (`rust_moon_plates()` /
  RUST_SKY_RAMP / RUST_MOUNTAIN_RAMP / RUST_CLOUD_RAMP, deterministic and
  idempotent): every pixel of the authored plate is luminance-gradient-mapped
  onto the rust family of the project palette (docs/art-spec.md, Void → Rust
  Shadow → Rust Dark → Rust Mid → Ember), the lower sky is eased toward rust so
  the horizon meets the graveyard warm, and the two violet cloud strips are
  remapped to soot → warm ash → dust so the overcast is lit by the rust moon
  instead of fighting it. Outline, alpha and size are the authored ones; no pixel
  is hand-painted and no external file is fetched.
- Ground contact for floor-standing carves (2026 follow-up to the user's floating-prop
  report): `set_pieces()` additionally gives `gh_furnace` a generated pixel stand
  (keeping its authored 32×96 canvas), stretches the `gh_skull_arch` legs to the canvas
  foot and lifts `gh_rock_pile`'s sparse bottom fringe onto a stone base value, so the
  visible silhouette touches the ground when the prop is pinned to a platform top.
  Still procedural/palette-only, deterministic and idempotent; no source pixels removed.
- Used: chapter 1 and chapter 6 (graveyard theme) backdrops, so the moon reads
  as a dull blood moon over violet-soot sky instead of candy magenta while the
  clouds belong to the same ash palette. The swap is gated on the graveyard
  theme id in scripts/levels/level01_parallax.gd and falls back to the authored
  magenta plates (with the old violet cloud tint) when a derived PNG is absent.

## Level01 graveyard set dressing — derived rust remains (project-original recolor)
- Local: assets/env/props/ground/{pipe_valve,broken_machine,girder_l,girder_r,fence,chain,bones}.png
- Derived from assets already listed above — no new source and no new download:
  - pipe_valve / broken_machine / girder_l / girder_r / fence / chain are the
    **Kenney** Platformer-Assets Request pack / Base pack originals (CC0, see
    assets/external/kenney/LICENSE.md) that `PropCatalog.DECOR` already points at.
  - bones is the Gothic Horror `gh_bones.png` set piece already generated from the
    **Ansimuz GothicVania Patreon collection** (see the character-art section
    above); its opaque tileset background is keyed to transparent here.
- Generated by tools/gen_theme_tiles.py (`rust_remains()` / `GROUND_REMAINS` /
  `GROUND_KEYED`, deterministic and idempotent): the Kenney pieces are
  hard-alpha-thresholded (no anti-aliased fringe, docs/art-spec.md), cropped,
  NEAREST-resampled to half resolution (1 art px = 1 world px, matching the
  cemetery sprites) and their luminance snapped onto a darkened rust ramp of the
  project palette (Void → Rust Shadow → Rust Dark → Rust Mid). No pixel is
  hand-painted and no external file is fetched.
- Used: Level01's `SceneDetails` set dressing (mid-climb bone pile, gate-approach
  broken brace, toxic-pit hanging chain) through
  `PropCatalog.path_for(key, "graveyard")` — the "ground" material-family folder.
  Other themes and other chapters keep the stock props, so no other level's art
  changes.
## Chapter 3-10 material families, set pieces and interior backdrop kit (derived, project-original recolor)
- Local (generated, all from sources already listed above -- no new download):
  - assets/env/{iron,basalt,rampart,nave}_slab_*/float_*/fill*.png -- per-theme
    terrain skins (Church Pack slabs/ledges + Castle/Horror brick, ramp-mapped).
  - assets/env/props/<family>/{slab,plate,rubble_dry*,balustrade,door_arch,statue,
    grave_cross,rock_pile,bones,life_remains,beam,beam_bolts,beam_narrow,
    metal_panel,pipe_valve,broken_machine,girder_l,girder_r,fence,warning_plate,
    chain}.png -- per-family prop variants consumed by PropCatalog.path_for().
  - assets/env/backdrop/{forge_sky,forge_far,forge_mid,forge_near,core_hall,
    wall_town,wall_clouds,tower_wall}.png -- per-theme backdrops.
  - assets/env/backdrop/{wall_iron,wall_forge,wall_core,wall_slate,truss_*,
    machinery_iron,machinery_forge,machinery_core}.png -- the interior vertical
    kit (seamless masonry wall plate, ceiling-truss silhouette band, floor-line
    machinery silhouette) for chapters 05 / 08 / 10 plus the cathedral vault.
  - assets/env/backdrop/{workshop_haze,workshop_far,workshop_near}.png -- the
    ansimuz CC0 industrial parallax pack re-mapped from green to the chapter's
    warm-iron identity (the raw pack is still shipped and is the fallback).
- Sources / licenses: Church Pack and Cemetery Pack (ansimuz, see above),
  Gothic Horror + Old Dark Castle + Gothic Castle (ansimuz GothicVania Patreon
  collection, see the character-art section), Kenney Platformer assets (CC0),
  ansimuz OGA industrial parallax (CC0). Nothing is hand-painted and no external
  file is fetched.
- Generated by tools/gen_theme_tiles.py (deterministic and idempotent):
  `gradient_map()` / `gradient_map_norm()` / `_snap_ramp()` put every pixel on
  the chapter family's palette ramp (docs/art-spec.md 16-color palette);
  `history_prop_variants()` hard-alpha-thresholds the 70px Kenney originals
  (no anti-aliasing) and halves them to 1x pixel density before snapping;
  `set_pieces()` flood-keys the Gothic Horror tileset's flat backdrop
  ((24,18,32) / (30,37,45)) to transparency so bones / skull arch / rock pile /
  furnace / toppled tower stop reading as pasted squares.
- Used: chapters 03-10 terrain, props and backdrops; `PropCatalog.THEME_PROPS`
  is the allowlist contract and `tools/gen_theme_tiles.py` is the only writer.

## Procedural boss soundtrack (project-original, procedurally synthesized)
- Local: `assets/audio/music/boss_*.ogg` — for every boss: `<track>_bed.ogg`
  (40 s drone/pad/percussion bed) + `<track>_hi.ogg` (second-phase layer).
  Campaign tracks: `boss_hollow_bell` (空钟, level02), `boss_capstan` (绞盘守渠人,
  level02b), `boss_choir` (无声唱诗班, level04b), `boss_bell_founder` (铸钟人,
  level07b), `boss_emberwind_herald` (炉风先驱, level09b), plus the existing
  `boss_executioner` (level01) and `boss_nightmare` (level10).
- Generated by `tools/gen_audio_music.py` (numpy/scipy DSP, deterministic and
  idempotent: every oscillator has an integer number of cycles per loop, filters
  and reverb run circular, so every stem loops seamlessly; levels are normalized
  per stem with ffmpeg EBU R128 — beds -19.5 LUFS, hi layers -23.0 LUFS).
  `Music.BOSS_TRACKS_BY_LEVEL` maps level ids to tracks (level-first, then theme).
- License: part of this project (CC0); no external samples are used.
